subject.title: sessions.create fork path has no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete

question: Should this public cross-plugin `sessions.create` transcript-fork and parent-link ownership gap be fixed through the normal public bugfix path, or routed through security-owned advisory/backport handling first?
rationale: The source evidence supports a narrow code fix, but the affected behavior is a stable gateway plugin-isolation boundary that can expose transcript content, so automation should not choose the disclosure and release-handling path on its own.

options.title: Approve Narrow Public Fix
options.body: Patch `sessions.create` to reuse the plugin-runtime ownership invariant before parent-linking or forking, then add focused denial and same-owner regression tests.

options.title: Route Through Security Handling
options.body: Pause public repair automation and handle advisory, disclosure, and backport decisions through the repository security process.

options.title: Declare Current Trust Model Intentional
options.body: Keep the current behavior only if maintainers explicitly decide plugin-runtime callers may read or link foreign plugin sessions and document why delete remains stricter.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Public Fix
recommendation.body: Patch `sessions.create` to reuse the plugin-runtime ownership invariant before parent-linking or forking, then add focused denial and same-owner regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Tyler is the strongest routing signal from parent-linkage and session-management history and also merged the PR that introduced the broad session APIs.
